title: Whooping cough PCR
what: This is a swab from the nose and throat that looks for the whooping cough germ.
why: For a long cough that comes in fits, especially in children, and after contact with someone who has whooping cough.
duration: the swab itself takes about a minute; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: How many weeks the cough has lasted
If you took antibiotics, and which ones
If you had whooping cough vaccines
If you were around a coughing child or adult

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not eat or drink for 2 to 3 hours before the swab. Children are usually asked to do the same. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Nose and throat
prepare.text: In the morning, do not gargle or use nose drops, unless the doctor said otherwise.

prepare.title: Antibiotics
prepare.text: It is better to do the test before starting antibiotics. If you already take them, do not stop on your own. Tell your doctor.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Tell your child a stick will touch the inside of the nose. It is quick. Hold them on your lap.

steps: The child sits on a parent's lap, and their head is held gently
A thin soft swab goes into the nose to the back wall
The swab is turned for a few seconds and taken out
Sometimes a second swab is taken from the throat
The swab is put in a tube and sent to the lab
feel: Unpleasant and tickly in the nose. You may want to sneeze
Your eyes may water. That is normal
A child may cry, but it all takes a few seconds
after: You can eat and drink right away
Until the result comes, try to stay away from babies and pregnant women
red_flags: The child stops breathing or turns blue during coughing: call emergency services
A baby eats poorly, is floppy, or vomits with the cough: see a doctor urgently
High fever and shortness of breath: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: When is the best time for a whooping cough PCR?
faq.a: The sooner the better, usually in the first weeks of the cough and before antibiotics. Later on, a blood test works better.

faq.q: Can you get whooping cough after the vaccine?
faq.a: Yes, but it is usually milder. Vaccine protection weakens over time.

reminders.text: Whooping cough swab soon. Do not eat or drink, do not gargle, and do not use nose drops.
